sentiment.instructions: Judge the attitude the tweet's author personally expresses. Pick positive or negative only when a clear, sincere emotion or judgment comes through. Default to neutral for facts, promotions, questions, plans, jokes and mild or mixed remarks.

criteria.positive: Clear personal enjoyment, love, praise, gratitude, admiration or eager excitement from the author: love, amazing, so happy, can't wait, best, thank you, <3, :). Warm wishes, prayers or blessings for people, including condolences that praise or bless the person, also count. An exclamation mark, an event, a win or good news alone is not enough.
criteria.neutral: Headlines and news reports, sports scores and results, event or product promotions and invitations, RSVPs, tickets, schedules, plans, questions, trivia, role-play or garbled text. Also covers mild or hedged opinions ('may be', 'not bad'), playful jokes, light self-deprecating humor (lmao, I'm dead, not ready, procrastinating), minor inconveniences said casually, and tweets mixing good and bad feelings without a clear dominant one. Negative words inside a quoted headline or a factual report do not make the tweet negative.
criteria.negative: The author sincerely expresses frustration, disappointment, sadness, anger, contempt or insults: hate, so sad, annoyed, worst, sucks, FML, :(. Includes hostile or mocking jabs at a person or group, bitter sarcasm, and complaints about missing out when the feeling is genuine. Also includes reports of clearly harmful events such as deaths, attacks, crimes, arrests and scandals.
